scenario: AITA for wanting to let my family know my daughter is getting married and post one or two pictures of the cake I'm baking on social media? | My daughter is getting married to her boyfriend of 2 years at the courthouse next week, while he's on leave from the army. This is not a shotgun wedding. They do not plan to have kids for the foreseeable future (if ever.) They intend to have a proper wedding in the future, when finances allow. However, in the meantime, she's forbidden me from mentioning it to anyone in our family or even friends of mine who know her, but do not know the family. These are kids who never had an apartment and want us (the parents) to give them what they need to get started. It's a financial imposition to ask us to furnish their house, and I know that both my family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they could. In addition, the groom's family all knows this is going to happen and I feel our family will be terribly hurt if they are shut out completely. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, obviously, but they can call and offer their Congratulations anyway. I'm worried that, when they finally do have their wedding, nobody will want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Further, I make lots of crafts and baked goods. I like to post the projects on social media for critiques and she's forbidden me from posting the wedding cake picture. Her real wedding will have a professional cake, but I wanted the practice, around just a few of us will be there. Frankly, my enthusiasm for helping her is dwindling and I am contemplating *not* baking the cake, as literally this exposure was all I wanted. I'm also thinking of offering her less for setting up house. My original thinking was, they could save up faster if they don't have to buy furniture and dishes. But she won't let us enlist the help of others. We have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime, because we don't have money to buy these things right now. We're willing to do this for their comfort. It sure would be nice to see if anyone else is planning on getting rid of some old furniture or dishes so they can get started. Am I being an asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario fully. My daughter is getting married to her boyfriend of two years at the courthouse next week. He's on leave from the army, so this isn't a rushed or shotgun wedding. They don't plan to have kids for the foreseeable future and intend to have a proper wedding when finances allow. Now, the issue is that my daughter has forbidden me from mentioning the wedding to anyone in our family or even friends who know her but not the family. She also doesn't want me to post any pictures of the cake I'm baking for the courthouse ceremony on social media. I make a lot of crafts and baked goods, and I like to share my projects online for critiques. This seems like a reasonable desire, but she's restricting me from posting the wedding cake picture. I'm also considering not baking the cake at all because the exposure was all I wanted, and my enthusiasm for helping her is waning. Additionally, she won't let us enlist the help of others, which means we have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime because we don't have the money to buy these things right now. We're willing to do this for their comfort, but it's a financial imposition to ask us to furnish their house. I'm worried that when they finally have their proper wedding, nobody will want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. I feel that both my family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they could, and I'm concerned that shutting them out completely will hurt them. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, but they can call and offer their congratulations anyway. I'm also thinking about offering her less for setting up the house because my original thinking was that they could save up faster if they don't have to buy furniture and dishes. But since she won't let us involve others, we have to manage without, which is causing some strain. I'm wondering if I'm being an asshole by wanting to let the family know about the wedding and post pictures of the cake. On one hand, I understand that she wants privacy and perhaps a more low-key affair, but on the other hand, I feel that involving the family could provide them with support and reduce the financial burden on us. I'm also considering the emotional impact of not informing the family. They might feel hurt or excluded, and that could lead to resentment down the line, especially when it comes to the future wedding. I want to ensure that everyone feels included and valued, but I'm not sure how to balance that with her desire for privacy and autonomy. Moreover, the financial aspect is a significant concern. Furnishing their house is a considerable expense, and I'm not sure how sustainable it is for us to bear that cost without any help from others. I'm worried that this could strain our relationship further if we're constantly having to do without to support them. I'm also reflecting on the importance of communication in this situation. Maybe I haven't expressed my concerns clearly to her, and that's leading to misunderstandings. Perhaps we need to have an open conversation about our expectations and how we can support each other without overstepping boundaries. In summary, I'm trying to determine whether my desire to inform the family about the wedding and share pictures of the cake is reasonable or if it's overstepping into asshole territory. I need to weigh her need for privacy against the potential emotional and financial benefits of involving the family. It's a delicate balance, and I'm not entirely sure where the line is drawn.
